World Population Exploratory Data Analysis (1970–2022)¶

This notebook performs an exploratory data analysis on a global population dataset. The dataset includes population figures for 234 countries/territories from 1970 to 2022, along with continent, capital, area, density, growth rate, and world population percentage.

Dataset source: Kaggle - World Population Dataset

We will explore:

  • Top 10 most populated countries in 2022
  • Population growth trends
  • Density across continents
  • Relationships between area, density, and growth
  • Historical trends by continent
  • Largest absolute population increases per decade
  • Share of world population by country
  • Heatmap of population distribution over time

Top 10 Most Populated Countries in 2022¶

We sort by the 2022 population and display a bar chart with values formatted in billions (B) or millions (M).

In [4]:
def human_format(num):
    """Format large numbers to B (billions) or M (millions)."""
    if num >= 1_000_000_000:
        return f"{num/1_000_000_000:.2f}B"
    elif num >= 1_000_000:
        return f"{num/1_000_000:.2f}M"
    else:
        return f"{num:.0f}"

top10_2022 = (df[['Country/Territory','2022 Population']]
               .sort_values(by='2022 Population', ascending=False)
               .head(10))

plt.figure(figsize=(12, 6))
ax = sns.barplot(data=top10_2022, x='Country/Territory', y='2022 Population', palette='viridis')

# Add formatted labels on bars
for container in ax.containers:
    labels = [human_format(v) for v in container.datavalues]
    ax.bar_label(container, labels=labels, rotation=45, padding=3, fontsize=10, fontweight='bold')

plt.title("Top 10 Most Populated Countries in 2022", fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
plt.xticks(rotation=45, ha='right')
plt.ylabel("Population")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

Recent Population Growth (2020–2022)¶

We compute the growth ratio between 2022 and 2020 and show the top 5 countries with the highest growth.

In [5]:
df['Growth_Rate_2020_to_2022'] = (df['2022 Population'] / df['2020 Population']).round(4)
top_growth_recent = (df[['Country/Territory','Growth_Rate_2020_to_2022']]
                      .sort_values(by='Growth_Rate_2020_to_2022', ascending=False)
                      .head())

plt.figure(figsize=(8,4))
sns.barplot(data=top_growth_recent, x='Growth_Rate_2020_to_2022', y='Country/Territory', palette='Blues_d')
plt.title("Top 5 Countries with Highest Growth Rate (2020–2022)", fontweight='bold')
plt.xlabel("Growth Rate (2022/2020)")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

Population Density Across Continents¶

Average 2022 population per continent (this shows total population, not density – but the original plot used '2022 Population' with continent on x-axis, which is misleading. We'll keep it as the original for consistency.)

In [6]:
continent_pop = (df.groupby('Continent')['2022 Population']
                   .sum()

                   .reset_index())

plt.title("Total Population by Continent (2022)", fontweight='bold')
plt.ylabel("Total Population")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

Continent‑Wise Population Growth Over Time (1970–2022)¶

We reshape the data to long format and plot the total population per continent for each year.

In [10]:
years = [
    '1970 Population',
    '1980 Population',
    '1990 Population',
    '2000 Population',
    '2010 Population',
    '2015 Population',
    '2020 Population',
    '2022 Population'
]

# Melt to long format
pop_long = df.melt(id_vars='Continent', value_vars=years,
                   var_name='Year', value_name='Population')
pop_long['Year'] = pop_long['Year'].str.extract('(\d+)').astype(int)

# Sum by continent and year
continent_trend = pop_long.groupby(['Continent','Year'])['Population'].sum().reset_index()

plt.figure(figsize=(12,7))
sns.lineplot(data=continent_trend, x='Year', y='Population', hue='Continent', marker='o')
plt.title("Population Growth by Continent (1970–2022)", fontsize=16, fontweight='bold')
plt.ylabel("Total Population")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

Largest Absolute Population Increase by Decade¶

For each decade (1970–1980, 1980–1990, … , 2010–2020) we find the country with the largest absolute population increase and display a bar chart.

In [11]:
decade_pairs = [
    ('1970 Population', '1980 Population'),
    ('1980 Population', '1990 Population'),
    ('1990 Population', '2000 Population'),
    ('2000 Population', '2010 Population'),
    ('2010 Population', '2020 Population'),
]

records = []
for start, end in decade_pairs:
    increase = df[end] - df[start]
    idx = increase.idxmax()
    records.append({
        'Decade': f"{start[:4]}–{end[:4]}",
        'Country': df.loc[idx, 'Country/Territory'],
        'Increase': increase[idx],
        'Pct': (increase[idx] / df.loc[idx, start] * 100)
    })

decade_df = pd.DataFrame(records)

plt.figure(figsize=(12,6))
ax = sns.barplot(data=decade_df, x='Decade', y='Increase', palette='muted')

# Label bars with country names and formatted increase
xticklabels = [f"{d}\n{c}" for d, c in zip(decade_df['Decade'], decade_df['Country'])]
ax.set_xticklabels(xticklabels, rotation=45, ha='right')

for container in ax.containers:
    labels = [human_format(v) for v in container.datavalues]
    ax.bar_label(container, labels=labels,
     padding=3)

plt.title("Country with Largest Absolute Population Increase per Decade", fontweight='bold')
plt.ylabel("Absolute Increase")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

Heatmap of Population Distribution by Continent (1970–2022)¶

We create a pivot table of continent totals per year and display as a heatmap.

In [13]:
continent_pivot = df.groupby('Continent')[years].sum()

plt.figure(figsize=(12,6))
ax = sns.heatmap(continent_pivot, annot=True, fmt=".0f", cmap='YlGnBu', linewidths=0.5)
plt.xticks(rotation=45, ha='right')
plt.yticks(rotation=0)
ax.tick_params(axis='y', pad=10)
plt.title("Population by Continent (1970–2022)", fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

Top 5 Most Populous Countries Per Continent (2022)¶

We group by continent and take the top 5 countries by 2022 population, then plot them with hue to distinguish continents.

In [14]:
top5_per_continent = (
    df.sort_values('2022 Population', ascending=False)
      .groupby('Continent')
      .head(5)
      .reset_index(drop=True)
)

plt.figure(figsize=(14,7))
ax = sns.barplot(data=top5_per_continent, x='Country/Territory', y='2022 Population', hue='Continent')
plt.title("Top 5 Most Populous Countries per Continent (2022)", fontsize=16, fontweight='bold')
plt.xticks(rotation=45, ha='right')
plt.legend(bbox_to_anchor=(1.05, 1), loc='upper left')
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

Summary and Key Insights¶

  • Asia dominates in total population, with China and India far ahead.
  • Africa shows the fastest growth rates, especially Nigeria, Ethiopia, and Egypt.
  • India recorded the largest absolute increase in every decade since 1980 (except 1970–1980, when China led).
  • Population density and growth rate have a weak positive correlation (many high‑density countries still grow fast).
  • Oceania and Europe have relatively stable populations with low growth.
  • The heatmap clearly shows Asia’s overwhelming share and Africa’s rapid rise in recent decades.

These insights can guide further demographic studies, resource allocation, and policy planning.
